skill.name: memory-systems

security_audit.summary: The system reconnaissance findings are false positives from memory graph identifiers, query examples, and prose. The external command findings are Markdown Python code fences, not shell execution. I found one medium privacy design risk because the skill promotes persistent personal memory without concrete operational controls.

remediation.issue: Persistent personal memory lacks concrete privacy controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent, retention, deletion, encryption, and access-control guidance before adapting examples to production systems.

remediation.issue: Reference implementations are educational and in-memory only.
remediation.suggestion: Document production requirements such as durable storage, audit logs, authorization checks, and bounded retention.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples triggered static command-execution detection.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that fenced snippets are illustrative examples and not installer or execution steps.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Personal Memory Lacks Concrete Controls
semantic_findings.description: The skill encourages long-term cross-session memory and includes examples involving a user address. The implementation stores facts with entity and session metadata, but does not implement consent, retention, encryption, or access controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly describe indefinite long-term memory, user address retrieval, and fact storage with session identifiers. This is a design privacy risk, not evidence of data exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Agents lose context between sessions and struggle to reason over changing facts. This skill guides memory layers, retrieval patterns, entity tracking, and temporal knowledge graphs.
actual_capabilities: Explains layered memory architecture from working memory to permanent storage.
Compares vector stores, knowledge graphs, and temporal knowledge graphs.
Shows retrieval patterns for semantic, entity-based, and temporal memory queries.
Provides Python reference implementations for vector and graph memory stores.
Guides consolidation strategies for outdated or conflicting memories.
limitations: The reference code is educational and not a complete production database.
It does not implement authentication, encryption, consent, or retention policies.
The sample embedding logic is illustrative and not suitable for production ranking.
It does not choose a vendor-specific graph or vector database for you.

use_cases.title: Build Cross-Session Assistants
use_cases.description: Design memory layers that preserve preferences, task history, and reusable facts across user sessions.

use_cases.title: Model Entity Relationships
use_cases.description: Use graph memory to track people, products, projects, and relationships that change over time.

use_cases.title: Improve Retrieval Strategy
use_cases.description: Select semantic, entity-based, or temporal retrieval patterns for complex agent workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Memory Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building an agent for [use case]. Recommend the simplest memory architecture that supports [session length] and [retrieval need].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Entity Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an entity memory model for [domain]. Include entity types, relationships, metadata, and retrieval patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design Temporal Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a temporal memory strategy for facts that change over time in [system]. Explain validity periods and conflict handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent memory design for scalability, privacy, retention, retrieval quality, and failure handling: [design].

output_examples.input: A user asks for an assistant that remembers preferences across sessions.
output_examples.output: Recommended design: long-term entity memory with preference records, timestamps, confidence, and retrieval filters. Add user controls for review and deletion.

output_examples.input: A team needs to answer relationship-heavy questions about customers and products.
output_examples.output: Recommended design: a knowledge graph with customer, product, and purchase entities. Use graph traversal for relationship questions.

output_examples.input: An agent must answer what was true at a past date.
output_examples.output: Recommended design: temporal relationships with valid-from and valid-until fields. Query only facts valid during the requested time range.

best_practices: Choose the simplest memory layer that satisfies retrieval and retention needs.
Store timestamps, source, confidence, and validity periods with important facts.
Define privacy, consent, deletion, and access controls before storing user data.
anti_patterns: Persisting every conversation turn without retention limits.
Using vector similarity alone for relationship-heavy questions.
Treating outdated facts as current without temporal validity checks.

faq.question: Does this skill install a database?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and reference code for memory architectures.

faq.question: Can it build production-ready memory storage?
faq.answer: It can guide the design, but production systems need security, durability, monitoring, and operational controls.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use a knowledge graph?
faq.answer: Use a graph when relationship traversal matters more than simple semantic document retrieval.

faq.question: When should I use temporal memory?
faq.answer: Use temporal memory when facts change and the agent must answer time-specific questions.

faq.question: What privacy work is still required?
faq.answer: Add consent, access control, retention limits, deletion workflows, and encryption before storing personal data.
